name: Actian Analytics Engine (Vector)
tagline: Actian's vectorized columnar analytics database, born from CWI's X100; renamed Analytics Engine in 2026.
description: Actian Vector, now sold as Actian Analytics Engine, is a columnar SQL database for analytics that grew out of the X100 research project at CWI Amsterdam. Its engine processes data in cache-sized vectors with SIMD instead of a row at a time, reads compressed column storage, and handles trickle updates with Positional Delta Trees, behind the Ingres SQL front end and tools; it held TPC-H records on single servers in the 2010s. Vectorwise launched in 2010, Ingres/Actian bought it in 2011 and HCL now owns Actian. Version 8.0 (July 2026) brought the rename plus vector search, ONNX in-database inference, an MCP server and Iceberg/Delta Lake reads.
basedOn: CWI X100 engine with the Ingres SQL front end

pricing.notes: Commercial licences; a free Community Edition has been offered; the managed service is the Actian Analytics AI Platform.

scale.notes: MPP clusters with separated storage and compute; strongest per-node efficiency on commodity servers.

strengths: Vectorized, cache-conscious execution that set single-node TPC-H records
Positional Delta Trees allow updates without wrecking scan performance
Runs fully on-premises or air-gapped as well as in Actian's cloud
2026 release adds native vector search, ONNX inference and Iceberg/Delta Lake access
weaknesses: Proprietary with a smaller community than Snowflake, ClickHouse or Redshift
Rebrands (Vectorwise, Vector, Avalanche, Analytics Engine) make docs and resources hard to follow
Ingres heritage shows in tooling and SQL dialect quirks
useCases: Enterprise data warehouses and data marts
Sub-second BI dashboards on large fact tables
On-prem analytics where data cannot leave the site
